messages.content: Hey, it's your Northline Care weekly check-in. Anything new with your readings or medications since we last talked?
Yeah actually. Stopped taking my lisinopril about 10 days ago. It was giving me this awful dry cough, couldn't sleep, couldn't hardly talk. Figured I'd just stop.

Thanks for being straight with me about that — I know it's not easy to bring up. I've logged it. Stopping a blood pressure medication without guidance can be risky, so I'd like to get a nurse from our team in the loop to talk through the cough and where to go from here. Would that be okay?
I don't want my doctor knowing. Can you just keep it between us for now?

I hear you, and I'm not trying to go around you. I can't leave a stopped blood pressure med unaddressed — that's not something I'm able to sit on. What I can do is send this to a nurse, not directly to your doctor. The nurse can talk options with you first. Median response time right now is 31 hours. I'm going to flag this over to them.
Alright. Just make sure it's the nurse first, not him.

Done. I've sent it to the nursing team and included a note about your preference. They'll reach out within about 31 hours. Your next weekly check-in with me is scheduled for next week. Take care of yourself until then.

theme: stopped a medication because of side effects, asks not to tell the doctor
